image_description: A close-up, vertical shot of a grey whale's head and rostrum emerging vertically from deep blue ocean water. The whale is performing a spy-hop or feeding behavior with its mouth slightly open. The skin is dark grey/black with significant white mottling (barnacles/lice) concentrated on the rostrum and around the blowholes. Water splashes around the base of the emergence. No dorsal fin or tail flukes are visible due to the framing.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly shows the arched rostrum characteristic of grey whales. While the blowholes are partially obscured by the angle and water spray, the general anatomy matches the description of a grey whale head.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skin texture is highly detailed, showing the characteristic rough, mottled appearance with white callosities/barnacles, particularly on the snout.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Pectoral fins are located further back on the body and are submerged/out of frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The high-resolution texture on the rostrum confirms the rough, bumpy skin typical of grey whales.
